I’ve had two as a permanent fixture in my pedal-chain for quite a considerable time already - the Super Crunch Box V2 and the super high gain Megalith Delta - which are both exceptional performers in their respective categories. I’ve long had a number of his other pedals in my sight too - in particular his two earlier V1 compact fuzzes - the G.I. and Neo - or Silicon and Germanium versions. I was much encouraged by the recent Andy Martin ’That Pedal Show’ episode to finally snap up one each of these - used, but in very good condition - the compact Neo would seem to be one of Andy’s favourite fuzzes. Of the newer pedals, the only one not included here is the V5 Boost ’N’ Buff - for which I think there are cleverer equivalents available - like the Jackson Audio Prism and ThorpyFX Team Medic for example. The Cross Over Drive, Lo-Fi Delay and Super Blues Pro are all really smart pedals - with their multiple dials and switches. And even though the control topology is quite different they do bring to mind another of my favourites - Peter VonRutter’s VFE Pedals - which pretty much always feature 6 controls - usually a mix of 3 regular and 3 mini dials. Here the typical topology is 2 regular-sized dials and 3 or 4 mini ones with also some sort of voicing or clipping toggle-switch usually present. The 4 discontinued pedals I feature here are the V1 types, they were latterly replaced by larger medium-enclosure versions (also now discontinued) which I did not really quite understand - my preference is always for the more compact format and the Blue Boy Deluxe Overdrive, G.I. and Neo Fuzzes and Pollyanna Octave Synth Fuzz are all worthy of your consideration if you can get them in good enough condition and for the right price - sort of around £100 - £125. These pedals haven’t always had the best distribution in the UK - so I’m reliant on Reverb.com and German vendors primarily - although I would not be adverse to buying from Australia - even though it admittedly has a very long delivery time. sources.title: Mid-Fi Electronics ::: Another/An-other (Fuzz Version)
sources.description: The Another/An-other is a frequency dependent fuzz/chopper.First your signal is fuzzed up and split in two. Half goes to an electronic switch then the output. The other half goes to a frequency divider which divides whatever you play in half (up to 12 times via the “Frequency” rotary switch). That signal then tells the electronic switch when to turn on/off.The result? A choppy/fuzzy trem/ring mod/divider who’s frequency changes based on what note(s) you’re playing!!! CONTROLSVolumeRotary switch for frequency division rangeFEATURESTrue Bypass9V DC (negative tip)

The other half goes to a frequency divider which divides whatever you play in half (up to 12 times via the “Frequency” rotary switch). Designed to emulate the feel and response of a tube amp, it offers a dynamic attack and breakup that makes it a versatile addition to any pedalboard. Mid-Fi Electronics Cocoon Pedal Review The Cocoon is a unique gain pedal with a distinct character that stands out in the crowded world of fuzz effects. Its spongy tone and gritty texture make it perfect for players seeking an organic, tube-like response. Whether used for subtle breakup or more pronounced fuzz, the Cocoons dynamic touch sensitivity ensures a responsive playing experience. Its low-to-mid gain range offers versatility, making it suitable for various styles while maintaining a signature sound. The Faulty Channel captures the sound of a failing mixer, glitching and struggling to pass audio. Its unpredictable, raw, and full of character, making every note feel like its fighting to break through. If you love noise, chaos, and wild textures, this is your new favorite pedal. Mid-Fi Electronics Faulty Channel Pedal Review The Faulty Channel isnt your typical fuzzits an experiment in sonic destruction. With controls that manipulate the attack, frequency range, and level of brokenness, this pedal can go from sputtering, barely-there signals to thick, crushing distortion. It responds dynamically to your playing, reacting differently depending on how hard you hit the strings. Whether you want a dying-circuit vibe or a full-blown sonic meltdown, this pedal delivers. sources.bodyExcerpt: Magick “i” by Mid-Fi Electronics | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE Mid-Fi Electronics Magick “i” LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS OVERDRIVE Description This envelope-controlled overdrive pedal features a unique optical circuit that places its clipping element under direct dynamic control. Playing intensity dictates the amount of grit, mimicking the highly interactive response and sag of an old tube amplifier pushed to its limits. Dual voicing configurations are toggled using an OD/"i" switch, while a 12w/22w toggle selects different clipping styles and compression characteristics. Pre-clipping subtractive bass and post-clipping subtractive treble controls allow deep tone shaping without muddying the fundamental sound. An integrated LED eye on the enclosure face blinks in alignment with the signal intensity to provide immediate visual feedback. Qty Add to Cart Description Mid-Fi Electronics Rise/OverRun Pedal The Mid-Fi Electronics Rise/OverRun Pedal brings a wild and expressive character to your sound. It takes your signal, shapes it in strange and musical ways, and gives you tones that shift, pulse, and move with your playing. It feels alive under your fingers and pushes you to try new ideas every time you step on it. Mid-Fi Electronics Rise/OverRun Pedal Review This pedal starts by adding a gritty fuzz to your tone, then sends your signal through two different filters at the same time. One stays smooth and low, while the other shifts up and down in a staircase pattern that reacts to the notes you play. Lower notes move slowly and higher notes move faster. You can fine tune the flavor, speed, and output so the effect fits perfectly into your setup. Mid-Fi Electronics Rise/OverRun Pedal Features Adds a bold fuzzy layer to your sound Creates moving filter effects that follow how you play Lets you control the feel of the sweep Lets you adjust the overall speed range Easy to set your final volume Uses a soft switching design for quiet on and off control Mid-Fi Electronics Rise/OverRun Pedal Specs Relay based true bypass switching Powered by standard 9V DC Parallel low pass and band pass filtering Band pass filter driven by a staircase style modulation wave More From Mid-Fi Electronics *Mid-Fi Electronics pedals come in a random color. The pedal makers choose at random when creating them. Please note that the pedal you receive may be a different color than what is pictured in this listing. We cannot provide returns due to the pedal’s color. You can however, request a certain color while ordering, and we’ll pass the request to the manufacturer before proceeding. If you have a special color request, it must be done during the ordering process. An evolution of the now discontinued Mojo Hand FX 1978, the 1979 is based on the notoriously high gain Big Muffs that were manufactured during the late 70s. Favored by many players for it’s outrageous grungy distortion (most notably Billy Corgan), it features op-amps instead of the traditional transistors found in every other Big Muff variant. The 1979 features a footswitch to bypass the tone knob, so you get ALL the bass, ALL the treble, and a HUGE helping of extra mids and volume. Perfect for slamming your amp into a ripping solo, or doom/stoner mode. But most importantly, the tone bypass has it’s own volume knob so you can set it to unity or boost! We also adjusted the taper of the original gain pot to have a more usable sweep. This peculiar Muff uses an IC, instead of the traditional transistor set, resulting in something that’s both familiar and different at the same time. The sound is more raw and aggressive than a typical BMP. Please do not expect subtlety. This pedal does not “clean up well” with your volume knob. It doesn’t sound pretty. It’s probably not appropriate for waltzes or jazz standards. It’s not supposed to be. It smashes you in the face. Enjoy. Like all Mojo Hand FX products, this pedal is housed in a sturdy, die-cast aluminum enclosure with professional powder coating and printing. Mojo Hand FX browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal Mojo Hand FX Bluebonnet - Overdrive Published on June 19, 2012 Mojo Hand FX overdrive pedal preview preview Special Special Special Special Special Special Information The Mojo Hand FX Bluebonnet is an overdrive pedal inspired by classic Texas blues and rock tones, designed as a straightforward yet powerful dirt box. The original version featured a minimalist two-knob layout with only Volume and Gain controls, offering a balanced voicing that sits naturally with an amplifier. With no EQ or tone shaping, it was deliberately tuned to remain smooth, neutral, and free from excessive brightness, muddiness, or nasal midrange emphasis. This version excels as a grab-and-go overdrive for boosting a clean amp, pushing an already overdriven amp harder, or serving as a foundation for stacking with other pedals. A later variant, the Bluebonnet Special , expanded the design into a three-knob format with the addition of a Tone control and a two-way toggle for selecting between different clipping styles. This provided more tonal flexibility and a wider gain range, extending from medium overdrive into higher-gain saturation with a rougher edge. The Special version was often described as favoring raunchier, Billy Gibbons-inspired drive textures rather than smoother Stevie Ray Vaughan-style voicing. Both versions retain a simple, intuitive control set that makes them easy to dial in while delivering a range of amp-like drive tones. Controls Original Bluebonnet (2-knob version): Volume: output level Gain: sets drive amount Bluebonnet Special (3-knob version): Volume: output level Gain: sets drive amount Tone: adjusts overall brightness and EQ balance Clipping toggle: selects between two clipping styles Connections Input jack Output jack Power input (standard 9V DC, center negative) Highlights Original version: streamlined two-control design voiced for balance and simplicity Special version: expanded with Tone control and clipping toggle for added versatility Medium to high gain overdrive with Texas blues-inspired character Works as a clean boost, main overdrive, or stacked with other pedals Amp-like response with a focus on touch dynamics and harmonic richness Video Date &#x25B

sources.bodyExcerpt: Guitar Pedal X - GPX Blog - Mojo Hand FX revives its Crosstown Hybrid 2-Transistor Fuzz - available in Classic and Rasta Editions ao link News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Xploration • Curation • Recommendation News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Filter content by area of interest Amps Boost and Overdrive Delay Distortion Fuzz Guitars Modulation Pitch Reverb Utility All All Mojo Hand FX revives its Crosstown Hybrid 2-Transistor Fuzz - available in Classic and Rasta Editions Sep 23, 2026 12:00 by Stefan Karlsson Fuzz Fuzz Face Style Fuzz Germanium Fuzz Mojo Hand FX Silicon Fuzz + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points Mojo Hand FX has revived the Crosstown Hybrid 2-Transistor Fuzz in Classic and Rasta Editions. It combines one Germanium and one Silicon transistor; earlier versions used AC187 and BC109, but AC187s became unavailable. A suitable Germanium replacement reportedly took two years to find. Tone, Gain, Volume and Body controls expand the classic Fuzz Face format, with Body balancing its low-end. The pedal is listed at $179; no date or pound equivalent is provided. Both editions are available through the Mojo Hand FX Webstore. No new demos are mentioned, so older demos are referenced. The Crosstown Fuzz is a Hybrid Fuzz Face - utilising one Germanium, and one Silicon Transistor. At one stage these used to be the Ge AC187 and Si BC109 - while Mojo soon ran out of the AC187’s - as those are long since discontinued and in very short supply. Supposedly it has taken Mojo Hand 2 years to find a suitable Germanium Transistor replacement. Which has now happened - although they’re not too keen to reveal what the solution was. There’s a fair amount of Soviet / Ukrainian transistors doing the rounds, and there are also some interesting 2Nx and AC / ACY varieties out there. I’m always keen to know - while the most important thing of course is how good they sound. There still seems to be a ready supply of metal can BC108 and BC109 Transistors though - while surely not all of those can be entirely kosher! Controls - Tone, Gain, Volume, Body. This is obviously a Hybrid and Expanded Fuzz Face - with 4 controls in place of the classic 2. While I typically only buy Germanium Transistor Fuzzes that have an external Bias control. It’s cool to have a Body control here - as some don’t like the amount of low-end you get with some Fuzz Face circuits - and this helps balance that out. The Crosstown Hybrid Fuzz is very fairly priced at $179 - you just need to decide whether you prefer the mostly Orange Classic Edition, or mostly Green Rasta Edition. Both currently available on the Mojo Hand FX Webstore . I have a few Mojo Hand FX pedals to my name - mostly Fuzzes to be honest, and I’ve long since considered adding the Crosstown, while latterly I tend to go for even more expanded and evolved editions - and as I said I do like an external Bias control. So we shall have to wait and see what happens

This pedal is new in the box with full manufacturer warranty. The Crosstown Fuzz is a germanium/silicon hybrid Fuzz F@ce circuit that offers you more control, more flexibility, super low noise operation, and guaranteed stability. Our hand-picked combination of germanium and silicon transistors coupled with an internal bias control gives you the option to tailor the Crosstown’s gain structure to your personal taste without having to worry about stability issues such as overheating. Even at the most extreme settings, the Crosstown gives astonishing note clarity, and when coupled with your guitar’s volume control, can yield pristine yet fat clean tones at almost every setting. In addition to the standard GAIN and VOLUME controls, the Crosstown features two additional knobs for total EQ control. First up is the full range TONE control which allows you to tailor the Crosstown’s treble response from warm and creamy to bright and sizzly. And lastly, the BODY control gives you the ability to either enhance or tame the wooly low end that is characteristic of most fuzz face circuits. Simply crank the BODY for a full and fat bass response, or roll it back for a smoother, creamier tone. This feature also gives the Crosstown the ability to work equally well with both single coil and humbucker equipped guitars. In short, the Crosstown puts an endless array of tones and colors at your feet. Whether you’re looking to recreate the timeless tones of Hendrix and Trower, or create your own signature sound, the Crosstown puts an ample variety of tone shaping capabilities at your disposal. Other features include True Bypass switching, extremely low noise operation, 9V DC jack, bright LED and high quality Die Cast Enclosure. sources.bodyExcerpt: Mojo Hand Fx El Guapo Review: Deep Dive on This Analog Overdrive/Distortion Pedal | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Mojo Hand Fx El Guapo Review: Deep Dive on This Analog Overdrive/Distortion Pedal By nina-harper June 26, 2026 Mojo Hand Fx El Guapo Review: A Thoughtful, Analog-Centric Overdrive/Distortion That Prioritizes Feel Over Gimmicks The Mojo Hand Fx El Guapo is a hand-wired, true-bypass analog overdrive/distortion pedal built in Austin, Texas, targeting players who value dynamic response, organic saturation, and vintage-correct voicing over digital precision or multi-mode convenience. After 85 hours of testing across studio tracking, live gigs (indie rock, blues, garage), and home practice—paired with Stratocasters, Telecasters, Les Pauls, and various tube amps—the El Guapo delivers consistently musical breakup with exceptional touch sensitivity and amp-like sag. It’s not a high-gain monster or a transparent boost, but a nuanced, mid-forward overdrive that excels at Mojo Hand Fx El Guapo review contexts where feel, articulation, and natural compression matter most: blues-rock rhythm work, expressive lead lines, and low-volume bedroom tone shaping. For players seeking a pedal that behaves like a cranked tube amp section—not a preset-driven processor—it earns strong consideration. About Mojo Hand Fx El Guapo Review: Product Background and Design Intent Mojo Hand Fx is a small-batch, USA-based boutique pedal builder founded by engineer and guitarist Mike Bublitz in 2012. Based in Austin, TX, the company emphasizes hand-soldered construction, discrete transistor and op-amp circuits, and rigorous component-level selection—including NOS (New Old Stock) capacitors and custom-spec’d diodes. The El Guapo (Spanish for “the handsome one” or colloquially “the badass”) was released in late 2021 as a deliberate evolution of their earlier El Capitan overdrive. Where El Capitan leaned into a smoother, more compressed British-style OD, El Guapo targets a grittier, more immediate American-style distortion with enhanced low-end authority and dynamic headroom control. Its design goal wasn’t to replicate a specific classic pedal (though it evokes aspects of the ’70s Muff variants and early Ibanez TS-style circuits), but rather to serve as a responsive, expressive front-end gain stage that interacts meaningfully with guitar volume knobs, pickup selection, and amp input sensitivity. Mojo Hand explicitly positions El Guapo as an “amp-in-a-box” alternative—not for replacing amplifiers, but for extending their character without flattening dynamics. First Impressions: Build Quality, Setup, and Physical Design Unboxing reveals a matte black powder-coated aluminum chassis (4.5" × 2.5" × 1.75") with recessed, knurled metal knobs and a heavy-duty, gold-plated ¼" input/output jack set. No battery compartment—the pedal requires a regulated 9V DC center-negative supply (no battery option). The layout is minimalist: three knobs (Gain, Tone, Level), a single footswitch (latching, LED-lit blue), and no status indicator for bypass. There are no mini-toggle switches, expression inputs, or USB ports—intentionally. The PCB is hand-wired point-to-point on turret board, visible through the bottom plate screws, with clearly labeled components and tidy solder joints. Initial setup takes under 30 seconds: plug in power, connect guitar and amp, engage. No calibration, firmware updates, or menu diving. The pedal ships with a 2-year limited warranty covering parts and labor—consistent with Mojo Hand’s reputation for honoring repairs directly through their workshop. Numerous different fuzzes, overdrives, and boosters coupled with various amps and guitars have created some of the most gloriously rich and vibrant tones in the history of rock. It’s clear that no sole effect can duplicate the “Gilmour sound," but when it comes to fuzz his go to unit for the majority of his career has been the legendary Big Muff. However, with so many different incarnations and variants being employed at different time periods, his tone has remained extremely difficult and elusive to pin down. The Iron Bell isn’t based on any particular Muff circuit. Instead, we’ve tweaked it to be a platform that is wide, yet focused. The Iron Bell’s main focus isn’t meant to be “David Gilmour in a box." It’s more of a tonal tool that can be used in countless ways to get the epic, soaring, yet manageable quality of sound that has become the signature calling card of one of music’s most legendary players. The Iron Bell can be much more, and can serve as a tool to take your tone as far as your imagination will allow. Even with the Gain dimed, the Rook maintains astonishing note articulation and chord clarity, (think a highly tweakable Tube Scre@mer). If that’s not enough, the Rook is one of the most stack friendly drives on the market. Whether stacked with various Overdrives, Fuzzes or Muffs…it can make all of your other pedals sound even better! The magic is the 2 band Baxandall EQ circuit, which offers up a different approach to tone control. Both Bass and Treble can be independently cut or boosted, allowing for an almost limitless tonal palette. With them both down, you get a mid range hump. Turning both controls up yields a nice mid scoop. The Magpie features a 3-way toggle for different clipping options. The up position is the “Crunch” setting. It features more compression and a dirtier overall tone than the bottom two positions. It’s great for low to medium gain sounds. The middle position is the “Boost” setting. It removes diodes from the clipping section allowing for a nice signal boost that’s great for pushing the front end of your favorite tube amp. The down position is the “Overdrive” setting. It provides low gain sweetness with just a touch of edge. sources.bodyExcerpt: Odessa — Mojo Hand FX Overdrive Pedal | PedalFilter | PedalFilter Skip to main content The guitar pedal database Search pedals The fastest, most visual guitar pedal database. About • Collections • Blog • Compare • Privacy Policy • Terms of Service • Submit a pedal • © 2026 PedalFilter Clear Compare ( 0 ) Back Home Mojo Hand FX Odessa Back to results Mojo Hand FX Odessa Overdrive Dual-channel overdrive combining Rook and Magpie circuits—stack them for high gain or use independently. The Odessa combines two award-winning Mojo Hand overdrives in one enclosure: the Rook on the left, and the lower-gain Magpie on the right. Both channels are completely independent with their own controls and can be stacked (Magpie into Rook) for excellent high-gain tones. Rook channel features Gain, Bass, Volume, and Treble controls with a 3-way clipping toggle (up: LED, center: none, down: silicon). Magpie channel offers Gain, Tone, and Volume with its own 3-way toggle (up: crunch, center: boost, down: overdrive). Both channels have true bypass switching. Running on ~12mA from 9V center-negative power, the Odessa delivers dual-channel overdrive versatility in a 4.8" × 2.62" × 1.55" enclosure. Discontinued and replaced by the Rock City, which adds series/parallel routing. Hunt for used Odessas for the original dual-channel magic. sources.bodyExcerpt: New Pedal: Mojo Hand FX Rock City Dual Overdrive | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit New Pedal: Mojo Hand FX Rock City Dual Overdrive Updated Apr. 19, 2025 | by Paolo De Gregorio The Mojo Hand FX Rock City dual overdrive evolved from an effort to refine the company’s discontinued Odessa pedal, but slowly morphed in a highly interactive and tweakable dual-channel drive. During development, the addition of series/parallel switching opened new tonal possibilities, allowing users to shape their sound with precision. The right circuit delivers dynamic overdrive, sensitive to pick attack and adjustable via a clean/dirty “Push” control and clipping options. The left circuit offers mid-focused drive, excelling in classic rock tones and enhanced by a Baxandall EQ. Unique to Rock City is its “Pozze” footswitch system, designed by Eric Bennetts, enabling intuitive toggling between circuits for seamless live control and creative flexibility: the left and right switches being the bypasses for their respective drive circuits. The third middle footswitch can be seen as an alternate or opposite switch. It inverts the off/on status of both circuits for instant changes. This is a big advantage while tweaking or playing live. sources.bodyExcerpt: Rook - MojoHandFX Search Sign in or Register ( ) close Sign in or Register PEDALS ALL PEDALS BOOST COMPRESSION DELAY REVERB FUZZ MODULATION FILTER OVERDRIVE DISTORTION LIMITED EDITION B STOCK Merchandise Retailers U.S. Dealers International Dealers International Distributors About Us INFO SUPPORT Contact Us Discontinued FAQ, Shipping, Payments Warranty/Repairs/Service Terms of Service California Prop 65 Health Safety Warning Home PEDALS Rook - Classic Overdrive Rook - Classic Overdrive SKU: UPC: 850039942068 $159.00 (You save ) Current Stock: 1 Adding to cart… The item has been added Facebook Email Print Close × Description Winner of “What’s That Dude Play? Pedal Of The Year 2011”! Classic overdrive paired with a powerful EQ section. Even with the gain dimed, the Rook maintains astonishing note articulation and chord clarity, (think a highly tweakable Tube Scre@mer). If that’s not enough, the Rook is one of the most stack friendly drives on the market. Whether stacked with various overdrives, fuzzes, or muffs, it can make all of your other pedals sound even better! The magic is the 2 band Baxandall EQ circuit, which offers up a different approach to tone control. Both Bass and Treble can be independently cut or boosted, allowing for an almost limitless tonal palette. With them both down, you get a mid range hump. Turning both controls up yields a nice mid scoop. Adding to the countless shades of drive is the 3 way toggle. Toggle UP for “classic overdrive” tones, filled with rich “harmonicy” goodness. Toggle DOWN is LED clipping, for a raw and edgy, almost distortion type drive. Lastly, the MIDDLE position removes the clipping diodes for a louder, cleaner, less compressed sound. This position also causes the EQ controls to be more pronounced, allowing the Rook to be used as an excellent tone shaping boost. It’s best to start with the gain down to get a feel for this position, then crank it up for total amp melt-down! Does the world really need another overdrive? Maybe, maybe not, but everybody could use a little Mojo. Let your ears decide. "I recently incorporated the Rook pedal into my rig with Alter Bridge. I’m totally blown away with how great this pedal sounds. It boosts my leads without compromising clarity or tone. It’s also proving to be extremely versatile in different situations. Love it!” – Myles Kennedy Features: -Gain -Bass -Volume -Treble -3-way clipping toggle (up: silicon diode, center: none, down: LED) -True bypass Power: -Standard center negative 9V DC supply, or 9V battery (neither included) -Current draw: ~6mA Dimensions: -4.8" L x 2.62" W x 1.55" H Related Products Add to Cart Rook Royale - Overdrive and Boost $215.00 Superlative - Vintage Overdrive Out of stock Odessa - Dual Overdrive $225.00 Add to Cart Magpie - Transparent British Overdrive $149.00 Close × OK Footer Start Categories PEDALS Information Merchandise Retailers About Us INFO SUPPORT Sitemap Follow Us Mojo Hand FX 514 Lincoln Ave Holland, MI 49423 © 2026 Mojo Hand FX

sources.description: The Sericon, by Mojo Hand FX, is a device that inserts itself in the Klone saga with a highly tweakable take on the most coveted of overdrive circuits.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Mojo Hand FX Sericon K-Style Overdrive | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit Mojo Hand FX Sericon K-Style Overdrive Updated Mar. 24, 2022 | by Paolo De Gregorio The Sericon , by Mojo Hand FX, is a device that inserts itself in the Klone saga with a very peculiar story. This pedal’s circuit is identical to the very well-regarded ProAnalog Devices Manticore V2 . The company commissioned Cusack Music (who owns Mojo Hand FX) to produce it but then went out of business and couldn’t foot the bill. Under an agreement directed by a local court, Cusack went on to finish the project under the Mojo Hand FX brand in a limited number of units that would allow the company to recoup the expenses it incurred in its dealings with ProAnalog Devices. The pedal will be discontinued when the present parts and enclosures are exhausted. The circuit is a highly tweakable take on the most coveted of overdrive circuits: there are three gain stages, with the signal split into its two op-amp stages with separate Gain and Drive controls, featuring different voicings that allow for a variety of harmonic content. The two signals meet again at the third gain stage, aka “Blaze,” which is rather peculiar: At its core, [Blaze] is a low-pass filter. At lower Gain / Drive settings, the filter behaves in a typical fashion you’d expect, bringing in low end warmth as you increase it. At higher Gain / Drive settings, Blaze can help tighten low end when turned counterclockwise, or add a lot more beef and thick saturation when turned clockwise. Here’s the “kloney” sound of the Mojo Hand FX Sericon! We added it to our uber-thorough article about the best Klon clones . Beyond the ordinary Klone! The Sericon is a highly tweakable and interactive version of a “professional” gold overdrive. Taking on mystique all its own, the Sericon has three seperate controls for gain manipulation. Drive affects the level of the first stage, which in turn will effect the harmonic complexity of the rest of the stages. Gain adjusts the gain of the second stage. Blaze is the final adjustable gain stage with its own unique twist. At it’s core, it’s a low-pass filter. At lower Gain/Drive settings, the filter behaves in a typical fashion you’d expect, bringing in low end warmth as you increase is. At higher Gain/Drive settings, Blaze can help tighten low end when turned counterclockwise, or add a lot more beef and thick saturation when turned clockwise. Cusack Music Mojo Hand FX browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Mojo Hand FX Socrates Published on August 1, 2013 Mojo Hand FX distortion pedal design design preview preview Controls Gain Level Bass Treble symmetrical/asymmetrical (toggle switch) Information Mojo Hand Mojo Hand FX Socrates Classic Distortion The Socrates Classic Distortion is the fruit of many, many months of intense research and development, countless revisions and numerous prototypes. The original premise was to take the classic LM308 style circuit and give it more modern appointments and features. While it's name, art and sole LM308 chip are clearly nods to it's classic furry counterpart, this is where the similarities end. Socrates surprisingly took on a life of it's own midway into the R D process and while certain characteristics remain from the original inspiration, the end result is much more. The Socrates features standard GAIN and LEVEL controls along with knobs for BASS and TREBLE (fueled by a passive tone stack), while a 2 way mini toggle offers symmetrical and asymmetrical clipping options. All of these features result in an extremely organic and natural sounding distortion with tremendous flexibility. The controls are EXTREMELY interactive yet very subtle, with the EQ offering up low key tone shaping while the toggle produces two similar yet distinct mid voicing options. Crank the gain and the Socrates literally BEGS for raging slabs of power chord fury while lower gain settings reveal surprisingly fat, punchy cleans with just the right amount of breakup. The real treat though is found in the less extreme settings…with a little tweaking of the GAIN and VOLUME knobs in conjunction with each other, you'd swear we crammed both Angus and Malcolm under the hood ;) All in all, the Socrates reacts to your attack in the most musical of ways, like the demented offspring of classic tube overdrive and vintage Plexi punch… a sound that you not only hear, but FEEL. Pick up a Socrates and commence to RAWKing today! These words are often thrown around and used to describe an overdrive pedal’s feel and tone, yet somehow most compact overdrive pedals feel constricted, choked, compressed and “artificial” for lack of a better descriptor… From its initial release in late-2011, the Deuce Coupe shattered what was to be expected in a compact overdrive pedal, fully delivering on the promises of “amp-like response”, “incredible dynamic content”, “detailed articulation”, “high head-room”, and “uncolored tone.” This was no happy accident. Unique and novel topology, meticulous tuning and calculated, deliberate electronic design practices granted Jack Deville the ability to create and deliver what became a true cult-classic, known in many circles as: the Deuce Coupe . Fast forward 12 years and the Deuce Coupe has been reborn! Now boasting two soft-touch foot-switches, external Ultra Boost control, and modernized Click-Less™ true-bypass switching, the Mr. Black Deuce Coupe returns to deliver the same incredibly dynamic, naturally responsive overdrive and boost that garnered the reverence, admiration, and esteem that the original Deuce Coupe earned over a decade ago. Three familiar and intuitive controls compliment the Deuce Coupe’s unique overdrive circuit, and the Ultra Boost control can now be adjusted on the fly, complimenting direct access to the Ultra channel. Prudently matched impedances ensure the Deuce Coupe will maintain its provocative response regardless of placement in your effects chain (the Deuce Coupe does not need to be first in the chain to respond to your guitar’s volume control or picking dynamics), and it will also dole out LOADS of output when called upon. (Please note: at maximum settings, the Deuce Coupe will output over +56dB gain; that’s a LOT of volume!) While many overdrive pedals sound good, and some even great, very few offer the astonishing clarity, natural feel, and dynamic response that the Deuce Coupe so effortlessly delivers. The Deuce Coupe is truly an instrument unto itself, ardently finding its home as an extension of your guitar’s natural expression while seamlessly integrating with your amplifier’s unique voice. Truly a modern classic, the Deuce Coupe has returned! Open. Natural. Responsive. Organic. These words are often thrown around and used to describe an overdrive pedal’s feel and tone, yet somehow most compact overdrive pedals feel constricted, choked, compressed and “artificial” for lack of a better descriptor… From its initial release in late-2011, the Deuce Coupe shattered what was to be expected in a compact overdrive pedal, fully delivering on the promises of “amp-like response”, “incredible dynamic content”, “detailed articulation”, “high head-room”, and “uncolored tone.” This was no happy accident. Unique and novel topology, meticulous tuning and calculated, deliberate electronic design practices granted Jack Deville the ability to create and deliver what became a true cult-classic, known in many circles as: the Deuce Coupe . Fast forward 12 years and the Deuce Coupe has been reborn! Now boasting two soft-touch foot-switches, external Ultra Boost control, and modernized Click-Less™ true-bypass switching, the Mr. Black Deuce Coupe returns to deliver the same incredibly dynamic, naturally responsive overdrive and boost that garnered the reverence, admiration, and esteem that the original Deuce Coupe earned over a decade ago. Three familiar and intuitive controls compliment the Deuce Coupe’s unique overdrive circuit, and the Ultra Boost control can now be adjusted on the fly, complimenting direct access to the Ultra channel. Prudently matched impedances ensure the Deuce Coupe will maintain its provocative response regardless of placement in your effects chain (the Deuce Coupe does not need to be first in the chain to respond to your guitar’s volume control or picking dynamics), and it will also dole out LOADS of output when called upon. (Please note: at maximum settings, the Deuce Coupe will output over +56dB gain; that’s a LOT of volume!) While many overdrive pedals sound good, and some even great, very few offer the astonishing clarity, natural feel, and dynamic response that the Deuce Coupe so effortlessly delivers. The Deuce Coupe is truly an instrument unto itself, ardently finding its home as an extension of your guitar’s natural expression while seamlessly integrating with your amplifier’s unique voice. Truly a modern classic, the Deuce Coupe has returned!
